metadata.title: Nutrition Guidance for Selected Health Conditions
metadata.purpose: Educational food guidance for a nutrition app. Not a clinical diet prescription.
metadata.review_status: Research-based draft; requires review and approval by a licensed dietitian/clinician before deployment.
metadata.language_note: Food examples are generalized and should be localized for Ethiopian foods, portions, availability, and preparation methods.

safety_rules: Do not diagnose a condition from food choices, symptoms, or user-entered measurements.
Do not use this file to prescribe calories, carbohydrate grams, sodium, potassium, fluids, or supplements for an individual.
Do not recommend stopping, changing, or adjusting medications.

If a user reports possible heart attack symptoms (chest pressure/pain, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, fainting, or pain spreading to arm/jaw/back), advise emergency medical help immediately; food guidance is not treatment.
For pregnancy, diabetes during pregnancy, complex diabetes, kidney disease, heart failure, or multiple conditions, recommend personalized clinician/dietitian guidance.
Food lists are not absolute prohibitions unless explicitly marked as pregnancy food-safety avoidances. Portion, preparation, medication, culture, and clinical context matter.

pregnancy.goal: Support maternal health and fetal growth through varied nutrient-dense foods and pregnancy food safety.
prefer: Variety of vegetables and fruits; wash produce thoroughly
Legumes such as lentils, peas, beans, chickpeas, shiro made with safe ingredients
Whole grains and higher-fiber starches such as oats, whole grains, and appropriately portioned injera
Well-cooked eggs, lean poultry/meat, and low-mercury seafood
Pasteurized milk, yogurt, and other pasteurized dairy or fortified alternatives
Nuts and seeds if not allergic
Folic-acid/prenatal supplementation only according to prenatal-care guidance
limit_or_caution: Foods and drinks high in added sugar
Excess saturated fat and frequent fried foods
Seafood choices and quantities: use local clinician/public-health guidance because mercury levels vary by species and region
avoid_food_safety: Raw or undercooked meat, poultry, seafood, and eggs
Unpasteurized milk and products made from it
High-mercury fish species listed by the relevant national guidance
Unwashed produce and unsafe food handling
app_rules: Never offer weight-loss plans during pregnancy.
Do not calculate pregnancy calorie or supplement prescriptions from this general guidance alone.
Ask trimester only if needed for a clinician-reviewed feature; do not invent trimester-specific nutrient targets.

diabetes.goal: Support blood-glucose management with balanced meals, appropriate carbohydrate portions, and personalized care.
prefer: Non-starchy vegetables (e.g., leafy greens, cabbage, tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots)
Fiber-rich, minimally processed carbohydrate foods in portions matched to individual needs
Legumes such as lentils, beans, peas, chickpeas, and shiro/misir
Whole fruits rather than juice most often
Lean proteins such as eggs, fish, poultry, and legumes
Unsaturated fats from nuts, seeds, avocado, and plant oils
Water and unsweetened beverages
limit_or_caution: Sugar-sweetened drinks, sweetened juices, syrups, and frequent sweets
Highly refined grains and large portions of starchy foods
Carbohydrate portions: do not assume all users need the same amount or must eliminate carbs
avoid_or_not_recommended: Do not recommend a very restrictive diet or elimination of all carbohydrates without clinician supervision
Do not suggest changing insulin or diabetes medication based on a meal recommendation
Do not label foods as universally forbidden; individualized carbohydrate management is important

components: About half the plate: non-starchy vegetables
About one-quarter: quality carbohydrate (e.g., legumes, whole grains, starchy vegetables, fruit, dairy)
meal_pattern_example.note: This is a visual starting point, not a fixed prescription; portions and carbohydrate timing may need adjustment for medications, glucose readings, and clinical needs.

app_rules: Do not let the AI calculate nutrition values; use verified database values and deterministic calculations.
Do not recommend fasting or meal skipping for users on glucose-lowering medication unless their clinician's plan specifically includes it.
If the user reports symptoms or a glucose value suggesting hypoglycemia, route to a clinician-reviewed emergency/low-glucose protocol rather than generic meal advice.
Offer clinician/dietitian review, especially for insulin users, pregnancy, kidney disease, or recurrent low glucose.

post_heart_attack_or_heart_disease.display_name: After a Heart Attack / Heart Disease
post_heart_attack_or_heart_disease.goal: Support cardiovascular recovery and long-term heart health. This is not treatment for an acute heart attack.
prefer: Vegetables and fruits in variety
Whole grains and higher-fiber foods
Beans, lentils, peas, nuts, and seeds
Fish and seafood as advised by the care team
Lean poultry and lean, unprocessed protein choices
Unsaturated plant oils in place of butter, ghee, and animal fats
Minimally processed meals prepared with little added salt
limit_or_caution: Sodium/salt, especially packaged, processed, preserved, and restaurant foods
Saturated fat from fatty meat, butter/ghee, full-fat dairy, coconut/palm oils
Alcohol; follow the cardiology team's advice, especially with medications
avoid_or_not_recommended: Trans-fat-containing foods; avoid industrial trans fats
Do not use diet as a substitute for prescribed cardiac rehabilitation, medication, or follow-up
Do not provide a personalized sodium/fluid target unless clinician-approved
app_rules: If heart attack symptoms are happening now or suspected, direct the user to emergency services immediately.
Label this mode 'heart-health / recovery nutrition' rather than implying foods treat or reverse a heart attack.
Heart failure, kidney disease, or fluid restrictions can change sodium and fluid advice; flag for clinician review.

hypotension.goal: Support hydration and symptom-aware eating while encouraging medical evaluation to identify the cause.
prefer: Adequate water/fluid intake if the person has no clinician-imposed fluid restriction
Small, more frequent meals if symptoms occur after large meals
Balanced meals; avoid skipping meals if that worsens symptoms
Foods providing vitamin B12 and folate as part of a balanced diet, when relevant to deficiency risk
limit_or_caution: Alcohol, which can worsen dehydration or symptoms
Very large meals if the user experiences post-meal blood-pressure drops
Salt increase: only if a clinician recommends it after reviewing the cause and other conditions
avoid_or_not_recommended: Do not automatically prescribe high-salt foods or salt supplements
Do not advise fluid loading when the user has heart failure, kidney disease, or fluid restriction
Do not treat fainting, severe weakness, confusion, or sudden symptoms with food advice alone
app_rules: Ask if symptoms are present and encourage medical assessment for recurrent dizziness, fainting, or symptomatic low readings.
Never infer that hypotension requires extra salt; cause and other health conditions matter.
If severe symptoms, collapse, chest pain, breathlessness, or confusion are reported, advise emergency care.
